items.title: The first-run authoring loop closes: package → object → record → app → publish → end-user, zero code, zero restarts
personas: admin (seeded admin@objectos.ai)
end user (same account driving the published app)

requires: a fresh boot of the showcase example — objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p <port> -d file:/tmp/<run>/data.db (the audit's environment: vendored console matching .objectui-sha, seeded admin admin@objectos.ai/admin123)
knownGaps: SUPERSEDED (QA run #24571): publish is no longer one click with no confirmation. Publish opens the 'Pending changes' review sheet — every pending draft listed as New or Update, each expanding into the keys it changes, and a separate 'Publish all' confirm (objectui app-shell preview/DraftChangesPanel.tsx, mounted by StudioDesignSurface.tsx; the audit's finding 3 / ADR-0016 §3.6 step 4). A review step now exists; do not score its presence or absence here — this item scores the loop

SUPERSEDED (QA run #21056): a new app no longer scaffolds zero nav items — the Create-app dialog seeds the app's navigation from the package's objects behind a checkbox that defaults ON (objectui StudioDesignSurface appAddObjects, objectui#2262). With it on, step 5's nav item already exists and the Interfaces step confirms it rather than builds it; only with it unticked does the manual wiring remain the contract. Do not expect zero items
mixed-language Studio chrome (audit finding 4) is asserted by i18n.studio-follows-app-locale — locale consistency is that item's business, not this one's

steps: boot the showcase example (objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin -p <port> -d file:/tmp/<run>/data.db), sign in as admin@objectos.ai/admin123, and note the boot timestamp in the server log (the zero-restart clause reads it later)

Home → 'Build an app' → Studio landing → create a NEW writable package (维修中心 / com.example.repairs, namespace repairs) via the new-package wizard. Type the identifier yourself: a CJK-only display name derives no package id (objectui PackageFormDialog.tsx toIdSegment: 'Empty when nothing usable remains (a CJK-only name, say)'), and the namespace derives from the id you type

Data pillar → new object 'Repair Ticket' (the identifier auto-suggests repair_ticket from the display name, and the dialog PREFIXES it with the package namespace, so the object is named repairs_repair_ticket — the name every later step and clause uses (framework#2694, objectui StudioDesignSurface prefixObjectName). The dialog also carries an OWD (sharing model) choice, pre-selected to the platform's recommended baseline: confirm or change it before Create) → add a picklist field Status with 3 values. There is no Save draft button: the designer autosaves, and a picklist field is held unsaved until it has at least one option (the status line reads 'Not saved yet: the field “Status” needs at least one option'), so add the field and fill its options, and the draft save fires

open the Changes panel and Publish, then confirm with 'Publish all' in the review sheet; the toast names the count — 'Published 1 item in this package (one atomic release)' (objectui#11807; 'Published all drafts in this package' is the fallback when the count is unknown)
create a record in the runtime-faithful Records grid with a Status value chosen
Create app 'Repair Center' (identifier auto-suggested) → Interfaces pillar → add a nav item bound to repairs_repair_ticket → Publish

return to the console Home (/_console/home — the Studio header's house icon goes to the Studio landing, 'Studio home', and the console Home is one click on from the landing's top bar): the launcher must show Repair Center; open it and drive the end-user list

verify server truth after each publish: GET /api/v1/meta/object/repairs_repair_ticket, GET /api/v1/data/repairs_repair_ticket, GET /api/v1/meta/app?id=<the new app NAME, e.g. repair_center> — ?id= matches the App document name, NOT the package id com.example.repairs; fetch /api/v1/meta/app with no query first to read the name the wizard actually minted

negative probe: on the READ-ONLY com.example.showcase package there is no gesture to drive — the console HIDES New object and Add field there (objectui StudioDesignSurface gates them on !readOnly) — so the probe is a FORGED request: send the authoring write the gesture would have made straight to the metadata write door against that package, and capture the server response (QA run #21056 read 422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED and 403 ITEM_LOCKED)

acceptance.clause: package create round-trips and the package switcher lists the new writable package without a page reload
acceptance.verify: the create POST succeeds and the switcher shows the package in the same session (objectui e2e/live/studio-object-designer.spec.ts test F1 is meant to pin it, but ⚠️ at the pinned objectui (.objectui-sha) it targets testids package-id-input / package-name-input that no source file declares, so it cannot be cited as a pass here; drive the clause by hand — and note the new-package wizard's own state, objectui#11327)

acceptance.clause: the published object is server-real: the meta read returns repairs_repair_ticket with the authored picklist field carrying exactly the 3 authored options — never ticked off the designer repaint
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/meta/object/repairs_repair_ticket body contains the Status field with its 3 options

acceptance.clause: the record entered in the Studio Records grid persists to the data plane
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/data/repairs_repair_ticket lists the record with the chosen Status value stored under the field's API name

acceptance.clause: the published app is live in the Home launcher and the end-user list renders the record with the picklist LABEL chip (label resolution, not the raw value)
acceptance.verify: launcher screenshot shows Repair Center; end-user list screenshot shows the record row with the label chip; GET /api/v1/meta/app?id=<the new app NAME> carries the nav item bound to the object
acceptance.evidence: the two screenshots + the app meta read

acceptance.clause: the loop closes with ZERO server restarts and zero code — publish alone made the package, object, and app live (the audit's benchmark: 'Zero code, no dead ends, minutes end-to-end')
acceptance.verify: the server log shows a single boot for the whole loop; no restart was performed between the first step and the end-user list
acceptance.evidence: server log excerpt spanning the run

acceptance.clause: the writable/read-only gate is enforced SERVER-side: the authoring write into com.example.showcase is rejected by the server even where the client lets the gesture through
acceptance.verify: the negative probe's server response is a rejection naming the read-only/installed-package cause (audit finding 1 proved this side holds); the client-side lock itself is access-security.readonly-package-locks-studio — cite a pass there, do not re-prove the DOM lock here

negative: silent acceptance of an authoring write into a read-only package is a FAIL (ADR-0124 D1 — the server is the authoritative gate; the client lock is courtesy)
a 'published' app absent from the Home launcher, or an end-user list rendering raw picklist values instead of labels, is a FAIL

items.title: Object designer round-trip: field add/edit/reorder persists to metadata, identifiers derive and survive typing
personas: admin

requires: a writable package to author into (create one via the Studio wizard or POST /api/v1/packages — the source-loaded com.example.showcase is read-only and rejects designer saves server-side)
knownGaps: AUTOMATION IS PINNED IN THE objectui REPO, NOT HERE — `automated.ref` names objectui specs exclusively, so from this checkout the item is neither runnable nor pin-evidenced (no console bundle is built here and none of those specs exist here). Drive it by hand in the browser and score it as a manual run, OR run the pin in an objectui checkout and cite the output naming the revision (17.1.0 sweep subject: 9a3daf8d37ad). ⛔ Never score it as covered on the strength of the `automated` field alone — an unrun pin is a claim, not evidence. Full protocol: RUNNER.md, the objectui-pinned-automation standing fact.

steps: open the object designer on the writable package: /_console/apps/setup/metadata/object/new?package=PKG (PKG = the writable package's id; note its namespace NS, from GET /api/v1/packages). ⛔ Not /_console/apps/com.objectstack.studio/…: the studio app is not loaded on a stock boot (RUNNER.md environment facts), so that route renders inside another app's chrome

TYPE the object name NS_repair_asset character by character (never .fill — the F2 per-keystroke-sanitisation bug only reproduces when typed) and confirm both underscores survive. The NS_ prefix is required: in a namespaced writable package the publish gate refuses an unprefixed object name (NAMESPACE_PREFIX). Type the name after the label, or re-check it before saving — objectui#12680: typing the Label after a hand-typed name overwrites it and drops the prefix
add a Text field, set its label to 'Asset Code', blur — the API name input must derive asset_code (F3)

add a Picklist field and author its 3 real options, THEN add one EMPTY option row; wait out the debounced live validation — no validation banner may appear for the empty row (F4). ⚠ Order matters: with NO real option yet the select-needs-options banner fires, legitimately — the empty rows ARE dropped, so the field has no options — which collides with a literal 'no banner' (and with objectui F4's toHaveCount(0) the same way). Assert the empty-row half with real options present

Save (the first save; the editor then autosaves every later edit — its Auto-save toggle defaults on, objectui ResourceEditPage.tsx metadata-admin:autosave — so later 'Save draft' steps are implicit), Publish; GET /api/v1/meta/object/NS_repair_asset and record the full field list and its order

reopen the designer: rename one picklist value, drag-reorder the fields (native HTML5 drag-and-drop: Playwright's dragTo moves a row, raw mouse moves do not — automation-input), let the autosave land, and Publish again
GET /api/v1/meta/object/NS_repair_asset again — the rename AND the new field order must be in the persisted metadata, not just the canvas
create a record via the Records tab and GET /api/v1/data/NS_repair_asset/<id> — the stored column key must be the derived API name (asset_code)

acceptance.clause: designer edits persist to the metadata store: added, edited, and reordered fields read back from the meta API exactly as authored — the designer repaint is never the oracle
acceptance.verify: before/after GET /api/v1/meta/object/NS_repair_asset: field set, picklist values, and field ORDER all match the authored state after each publish

acceptance.clause: a new field's API name derives from its label on blur, so the data column is the derived name — never a frozen field_N (the contract behind audit finding 2, where the saved record stored 'field_2': 'in_progress' forever)
acceptance.verify: the field-apiname input shows asset_code after the label blur (pinned by objectui F3), and the stored record's column key is asset_code

acceptance.clause: typed identifiers survive per-keystroke sanitisation — NS_repair_asset keeps its underscores when typed char-by-char
acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms the designer rendered, the name input's value equals the typed NS_repair_asset, character for character (pinned by objectui F2; pre-fix repair_asset yielded 'repairasset')

acceptance.clause: an empty picklist option row does not trip spec validation (no developer-facing 'System identifier must be at least 2 characters' banner) — judged with the 3 real options already present, because a picklist holding only empty rows legitimately raises the select-needs-options banner — while the PUBLISHED picklist carries exactly the 3 authored options
acceptance.verify: with the 3 real options present, no metadata-validation-banner after the debounce once the empty row is added (F4's negative assertion, read in that order), and the meta read shows 3 options — the empty row was dropped, not persisted. A select-needs-options banner shown BEFORE any real option exists is correct and is not this clause's FAIL

negative: an API name frozen at field_N after its label was set pre-save is audit finding 2 regressed — FAIL, but confirm against a fresh objectui build first: the vendored /_console bundle may predate the derive-on-blur fix the e2e now pins

items.title: List + form view authoring goes live in the running app on publish — no server restart
personas: admin (authors)

end user (consumes the published views). A runtime-authored object grants no non-admin persona any access, so a non-admin list render needs a permission-set grant on it first; without one, score the end-user surfaces as the admin and say so (QA run #24571)

requires: a runtime-authored object in a writable package to bind views to (e.g. repair_asset from studio-authoring.object-designer-roundtrip), so no shipped showcase view is mutated. The object must declare a `sharingModel`: its draft PUT answers 200 without one, but publish refuses it (security-owd-unset, error tier — packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts), so an object authored without it never goes live (QA run #24571)

steps: author a view CONTAINER draft via the metadata draft door: PUT /api/v1/meta/view/qa_repair_asset_views?mode=draft with { object: 'repair_asset', list: { type: 'grid', columns: [...] }, form: { ... } } — the container's own keys are list/form/listViews/formViews (ViewSchema); capture the receipt
as an end user, open the object's list BEFORE publishing: it must still render the previously published views (or the synthesized default) — the draft is staged only
publish: POST /api/v1/meta/view/qa_repair_asset_views/publish

reload the app page (client reload allowed, NO server restart): the list must render the authored column set; open New or Edit on a record: the authored form view layout applies in those dialogs (opening a record shows its record page, not the form view)
read back through the consumer door: GET /api/v1/meta/view?object=repair_asset (the getViewsByObject read) returns the container
edit the list view — reorder the columns and add one — re-publish, reload, and re-screenshot
capture the server log across the whole sequence (the no-restart clause reads it)

acceptance.clause: the draft save answers 200 with state:'draft' and a version (the ADR-0008 OCC token) in the receipt
acceptance.verify: SaveMetaItemResponse fields per packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts: success, version, seq, state:'draft'

acceptance.clause: pre-publish, end-user surfaces still serve the last ACTIVE views — the draft is invisible ('a draft is staged only — it is not served to the runtime until published')
acceptance.verify: the end-user list rendered before publish shows the OLD columns; pair with a GET of the view name showing no draft leakage

acceptance.clause: post-publish, the list renders the authored columns and the form renders the authored layout with NO server restart — a client page reload is the documented semantics (the audit's whole loop closed live inside one server session)
acceptance.verify: post-publish screenshots show the new list columns and form layout; the server log shows no restart between draft, publish, and render

acceptance.clause: the published container round-trips through the consumer read door
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/meta/view?object=repair_asset includes the container's EXPANDED items — repair_asset.default (list) and repair_asset.form (form) — carrying the authored list/form config. The object door never returns the container under its own name (expandViewContainer, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts; #7163, #7736, #13407), so the container name's absence is not a fail; an expanded item missing or carrying the old config is

acceptance.clause: edit + re-publish updates the live list (new column order renders) — the authoring loop is repeatable, not create-only
acceptance.verify: the second-publish screenshot shows the reordered/extended columns

negative: a view change that needs a SERVER restart to appear is a FAIL against the audit's zero-restart benchmark

a draft's columns leaking into the end-user list before publish is a lifecycle FAIL (the full draft→publish contract is studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle — this item only asserts the view-flavored live side)

items.title: Metadata draft→publish lifecycle: drafts staged not served, publish flips visibility atomically, conflicts and invalid drafts refused, and the history/audit/diff/rollback forensics tell the truth
personas: admin (authors drafts)
end user (must not see drafts)

requires: scratch metadata names only (e.g. qa_lifecycle_probe) via the draft door PUT /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name>?mode=draft — no shipped showcase file is touched
a writable package with two stageable drafts for the package-wide publish-drafts door
knownGaps: NO PIN COVERS A FULL CLAUSE — `automated` was dropped at revision 8, so this P1 item is hand-driven (Tier 2). packages/qa/dogfood/test/dashboard-designer-roundtrip.dogfood.test.ts, the pin it cited, saves a layout-less dashboard as a draft (PUT ?mode=draft answers 200), publishes it (200) and reads it back as { type, name, item } with its three widgets. That is acceptance[1]'s post-publish half and nothing more: it asserts no state:'draft' receipt and makes no pre-publish read (acceptance[0], and acceptance[1]'s never-served half), and it probes none of acceptance[2]–[11]: no second draft, stale If-Match, publish-drafts batch, invalid draft, Studio chrome, history, diff, rollback, audit or X-Actor. So it scores no clause (Tier 1 run #24598: every clause not-run). Re-add `automated` only with a pin that asserts a full clause.

steps: author a dashboard draft: PUT /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe?mode=draft with one dataset-bound widget (dataset: showcase_task_metrics, dimensions: ['status'], values: ['task_count']) — the same door areas/dashboards.json exercises
record the receipt: { success, version, seq, state: 'draft' }

BOTH sides pre-publish: GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe as the runtime read → 404 (never published) — the draft body must not be served; in Studio the item header shows the draft line 'Draft · N unpublished' (objectui#12725, studioItemDraftStatus.ts; N is the package's pending count) and a numbered pill on the Changes button (objectui#12459). For the Studio half stage the draft in a WRITABLE package (?package=PKG on the draft PUT): the pill counts the pending drafts of the package in scope, and an env-wide, package-less draft is counted in no package scope, so it shows no pill. Open the item in Studio through that package: stage, in the same package, an app draft whose navigation names the dashboard (e.g. an entry of type dashboard, dashboardName qa_lifecycle_probe) and select that entry in the Interfaces pillar — a package with no app shows 'This package has no app yet' and no dashboard to select, so no chip can render; the pill then counts both drafts
publish per-ref: POST /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/publish → 200; GET now serves the authored body
author a SECOND draft revision on the same name and confirm the live read keeps serving revision 1 until that draft is published
concurrency guard: re-PUT with the STALE version as If-Match and capture the 409

package-wide door: stage two drafts in the writable package and POST /api/v1/packages/<pkg id>/publish-drafts — both flip in one atomic release (the audit's 'Published all drafts in this package (one atomic release)' toast); capture the STATUS and the BODY separately, because the abort path answers 200 with data.success:false (see the clause below)
author an INVALID draft (a widget carrying a stray legacy key) and attempt its publish — the author-time gate must reject the draft→active transition (#4463)

meta forensics (after the two publishes of qa_lifecycle_probe — revision 1, then the second revision): GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/history — the durable sys_metadata_history events must list BOTH published revisions (a dashboard is an overlay type, so history is real; a non-overlay type answers { events: [] } by design). History counts draft saves AND publishes, so two save-draft-then-publish rounds read v1 (draft), v2 (its publish), v3 (draft), v4 (publish): read the two PUBLISH versions off this body for the diff step, steps[9] (QA run #23166 read v2 and v4)

GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/diff?from=<first publish version>&to=<second publish version> — the two publish versions read off /history in steps[8] (v2 and v4 on a clean two-round run); the structural diff must name the widget key that changed between the revisions, not dump the whole body. ⛔ Not ?from=1&to=2: v1 → v2 is a draft save and its own publish, which differ in nothing (changed []), and a default previous-vs-current read can land on the same draft/publish pair

POST /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/rollback with { toVersion: 1 }, driven under an authenticated session so the actor is attributable — the authenticated identity is the ONLY source ([#7941]; resolveMetaWriteActor no longer consults `X-Actor` at all); the runtime GET must then serve revision 1's body again and the rendered dashboard must show revision 1's widget

repeat the rollback (or another /meta write on this item, e.g. a follow-up draft save) while ALSO sending header `X-Actor: someone_else_entirely` on the authenticated request — the header must NOT change the recorded actor: the audit/history rows for that action still name the authenticated runner's own identity, never `someone_else_entirely` ([#7941] — pinned at the unit layer in packages/rest/src/meta-write-actor-identity.test.ts)
attempt a rollback with a missing/invalid toVersion and capture the 400 INVALID_REQUEST guard

GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/audit — the save/publish/rollback rows must carry the acting user; run every forensics probe against the REST route-manager server os dev serves, NEVER a simulated dispatch (the dispatcher /meta branch swallows /history as a compound name and 404s)

acceptance.clause: a draft save answers state:'draft' and is staged only — the runtime read does not serve it (both sides captured: receipt + 404/last-active read)
acceptance.verify: PUT receipt has state:'draft' (SaveMetaItemResponseSchema); the follow-up GET returns 404 (or the last ACTIVE body for a previously-published name), never the draft body

acceptance.clause: publish flips visibility exactly once: the post-publish read serves the authored body; the pre-publish read never did
acceptance.verify: POST /meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/publish → 200, then GET returns { type, name, item } with the widget intact

acceptance.clause: a pending second draft does not perturb the live revision until published
acceptance.verify: after staging draft 2, GET still returns revision 1's body; after publishing draft 2, GET returns revision 2

acceptance.clause: optimistic concurrency holds: a write carrying a stale If-Match version answers 409 metadata_conflict — a concurrent edit is reported, never silently overwritten
acceptance.verify: re-PUT with the superseded version token → 409 with the metadata_conflict code (the ADR-0008 chain the receipt's version field exists for)

acceptance.clause: package-wide publish-drafts promotes every pending draft in one atomic release — and a non-compliant draft (e.g. an object draft missing the package namespace prefix) aborts the batch BEFORE any promotion
acceptance.verify: POST /api/v1/packages/<id>/publish-drafts flips both staged drafts; the namespace-gate rejection path leaves ALL drafts unpromoted (packages/objectql/src/protocol-publish-package-drafts.test.ts pins the atomicity). ⚠ SCORE THE ABORT OFF THE BODY, NOT THE STATUS (run #7695): the namespace-gate abort answers HTTP 200 with data.success:false, so a status-only assertion reads an aborted publish as a successful one. Read data.success and then prove the atomicity — the run verified the abort leaves BOTH names 404. Whether 200+success:false or a 4xx is the intended contract for this door is an OPEN LEDGER QUESTION recorded at #7753 item 2, awaiting one deliberate ruling; until it is ruled, assert the CURRENT behaviour and do not file the status code as a defect
acceptance.evidence: the publish-drafts response (status AND body) + post-state reads showing both names still 404

acceptance.clause: an invalid draft cannot cross into active: the author-time rules gate the draft→active transition (#4463) — publish of the stray-key draft is refused
acceptance.verify: the publish attempt on the invalid draft errors; the live read still serves nothing (or the prior good revision)

acceptance.clause: Studio chrome tells the truth: the item header's 'Draft · N unpublished' line and the numbered pill on the Changes button while pending, cleared after publish
acceptance.verify: for a draft staged in a writable package (an env-wide draft is counted in no package scope, so it shows no pill): the draft line and the pill visible pre-publish, both gone post-publish and after a reload. A publish made outside Studio (the REST publish of steps[3]) shows in Studio only after a reload; Studio's own 'Publish all' clears them at once (QA run #24604) (the audit found this model 'reads consistently everywhere')

acceptance.clause: the durable history lists BOTH published revisions after two publishes — GET /meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/history returns the sys_metadata_history events for revision 1 and revision 2 (real events because a dashboard is an overlay type; a non-overlay type returning { events: [] } is by design, not a miss)
acceptance.verify: the /history body carries the two PUBLISH events with ascending seq/version, among the draft-save events history also records (v1 draft, v2 publish, v3 draft, v4 publish on a clean two-round run) — consulted on the REST route-manager server, not the dispatcher

acceptance.clause: diff names the changed key, not a whole-body dump — GET .../diff between the two PUBLISH versions read off /history (v2 → v4 on a clean run) isolates the widget/dimension key that differs between the two revisions
acceptance.verify: the diff body reports the changed path (the edited widget key), not the entire document; a diff of a draft save against its own publish (from=1&to=2) reports changed [] and scores nothing either way

acceptance.clause: rollback restores revision 1 AND the live app serves it — POST .../rollback { toVersion: 1 } → 200, the runtime GET then serves revision 1's body, and the rendered dashboard shows revision 1's widget; a missing/invalid toVersion answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST, never a silent no-op
acceptance.verify: post-rollback GET /meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe returns revision 1's body (a screenshot of the reverted widget corroborates the served side); the bad-toVersion attempt returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST
acceptance.evidence: the rollback response + the post-rollback GET + the reverted-render screenshot + the 400 response

acceptance.clause: audit rows carry the actor — GET .../audit lists the save/publish/rollback attempts (allowed and denied) each stamped with the acting user, resolved from the authenticated session identity ([#7941] — the sole source; `resolveMetaWriteActor` no longer reads `X-Actor` at all), never anonymous
acceptance.verify: the /audit body's rows for this name include the publish and rollback actions with a non-empty actor field

acceptance.clause: X-Actor is inert on an authenticated /meta write: sending the header does NOT change the recorded actor — the authenticated identity is stamped either way ([#7941])
acceptance.verify: repeat an authenticated /meta write on this item (e.g. the rollback POST) with header X-Actor: someone_else_entirely added; the follow-up GET .../audit and GET .../history rows for that action name the authenticated runner's own identity, and `someone_else_entirely` appears in neither row
acceptance.evidence: the X-Actor-bearing request + the audit/history rows for that action, showing the authenticated actor and the absent header value

negative: a draft body served to end users before publish is the lifecycle FAIL this item exists for

a publish that answers 200 while the live read still serves the old body is a FAIL — the ADR-0045 visibility flip failing loudly is exactly the path packages.ts warns about, and silence there is worse than the warning

a forensics route consulted on the dispatcher instead of the REST route-manager server is a recording error — the dispatcher /meta branch swallows /history as a compound name and 404s (rest-route-ledger.ts note); the oracle is the live server os dev serves
a rollback that answers 200 while the live read still serves the newer revision is a FAIL (the restore must actually flip the served body)

OPEN LEDGER QUESTION, not a verdict (run #7695 → #7753 item 2): publish-drafts' namespace-gate abort answers HTTP 200 with data.success:false rather than a 4xx. The envelope-level success flag may well be the intended contract for this door, and the atomicity behind it is correct (the abort leaves both names 404) — but an HTTP-status-only client reads an aborted publish as a successful one, which is why it is worth ONE deliberate ruling. Recorded here so the observation is not re-derived every run; a runner does not adjudicate it and does not score it as a FAIL

items.title: An invalid authored shape is rejected at save with a LOCATED error and is not persisted
personas: admin

requires: scratch metadata names only (qa_invalid_probe / qa_invalid_views) — rejected drafts must leave nothing behind, so no cleanup dependency
knownGaps: KNOWN SPURIOUS BANNER — do not file it as new (run #7695's sighting recorded here so it is not re-filed a third time): a freshly saved VALID draft can show "Unrecognized key(s) on this object: `_diagnostics`". The designer re-validates the server's OWN annotation on read-back — `_diagnostics` is added by the server to the saved body, and the strict client-side schema then rejects it. It is a false positive on a save that succeeded, and it is the exact inverse of what this item asserts (a LOCATED error on an INVALID shape), so it is worth telling apart on sight: if the banner names `_diagnostics` and the save returned 2xx, it is this known issue, not a validation failure

steps: attempt PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_invalid_probe?mode=draft with a field MISSING its type; capture the status and full error body

attempt PUT /api/v1/meta/view/qa_invalid_views?mode=draft with `type`/`columns` at the CONTAINER level (the flat-list-view mistake) BESIDE a container key (e.g. `list: {…}`), so the body is container-shaped and the container's guidance answers; capture the guidance error. A body of `type`/`columns` alone is judged as an inline view config instead and refused as naming no `object`/`viewKind` — the same 'Wrap it: defineView({ list: … })' remedy, different first sentence (packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts INLINE_VIEW_OBJECT_REQUIRED / INLINE_VIEW_KIND_REQUIRED)
after each rejection, GET the name back and record what the store holds

drive one invalid shape through the browser door that reaches the server gate — the Setup metadata editor's Source tab (/_console/apps/setup/metadata/object/NAME), whose autosave PUTs it — and capture the surfaced error. The Studio designer holds an incomplete shape client-side and never sends it ('Not saved yet: …'), so it does not exercise the 422 — it must locate the offending field, not say a generic 'save failed'
author the CORRECTED shapes (field with a type; views wrapped under list:) and confirm both save 200 — the gate rejects the shape, not the name
dashboard-kind stray keys are deep-covered by dashboards.strict-widget-rejects-stray-keys — cite a pass there rather than re-enumerating the 11 legacy keys here

acceptance.verify: the rejection is 4xx and its body names the exact field path that failed spec validation

an object with MORE THAN 6 fields to expand in the matrix, so the field sub-table's filter renders (FieldsSubTable shows the filter only when fields.length > 6) — a stock showcase object with a wide field set (showcase_account / showcase_invoice) on the environment door, or an object OF THE PACKAGE in the Studio Access pillar: in package scope the matrix lists only the package's own objects (objectui PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx, 'In package scope, list only the objects this package declares'), so a scratch package's set reads '0 objects granted' even when it grants showcase_account (QA run #24604)

steps: open the Permission Matrix editor on a writable permission set (Studio Access pillar, or /_console/apps/com.objectstack.studio/metadata/permission/<name>); expand an object with > 6 fields so the field sub-table's filter renders (threshold is > 6)

B4 field filter: type a filter that narrows the field set to a couple of fields; confirm the sub-table's 'n / N' counter and the DOM show only the matching fields (the hidden fields' read/edit checkboxes are absent)

B4 bulk-over-visible: click 'Write all' (perm.field.bulk.writable) → it must grant read+write to EXACTLY the visible fields; clear the filter and confirm the previously-hidden fields are UNTOUCHED (still at their prior grant), never bulk-applied

on a different filtered set click 'Read all' → it revokes write on the visible fields only; click 'Clear' → it drops the explicit overrides so the visible fields fall back to the read-only default (readable, not editable)

Save; GET /api/v1/meta/permission/<name> (or the package draft read) and assert the fields map (keyed `${object}.${field}`) carries overrides for ONLY the fields that were visible when each bulk fired — never a filter-hidden field

B3 clip: shrink the viewport to a narrow width; confirm the object matrix's enclosing overflow-auto container SCROLLS horizontally (the table carries min-w-[960px]) and the Bulk column (Read / CRUD / All / None per row) stays reachable, not clipped off the right edge

the grant→access flip (a flipped verb actually changing a persona's API access) is access-security.permission-matrix-edit-loop — cite a pass there; this item does NOT re-prove that a saved grant changes access

items.title: Source-authored page tiers render by the RIGHT path: kind:'html' source is PARSED-never-executed (static, in-browser sdui-parser compile), kind:'react' source is EXECUTED behind its capability gate (live data + interactivity) — command-center-jsx / capability-map (html) vs crm-workbench (react)
personas: admin (seeded admin@objectos.ai) driving the published showcase app as an end user

requires: seeded showcase_project rows (the react page's live KPI + <ListView> read them)
the react-pages capability ON — CAP_REACT_PAGES defaults ON; a boot with OS_PAGE_REACT=off flips it OFF (the both-sides gate check)
knownGaps: NO manual build step is needed to VIEW either tier in the running showcase (contra the task's guess): a kind:'html' page compiles IN-BROWSER via @object-ui/sdui-parser compile(source, manifest) at render, against a whitelist manifest built from the LIVE ComponentRegistry (packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx); a kind:'react' page is transpiled IN-BROWSER by a lazily-loaded Sucrase @object-ui/react-runtime chunk. The only build-shaped risk is the vendored /_console bundle being stale (stale-console-bundle) — a stale sdui-parser/react-runtime mis-compiles a page that is fine on a fresh build. ⚠ A FAULTING html source never reaches the RENDERED page on a stock boot: the metadata save door compiles an html page's source against the deployment's manifest with the same compiler `os validate` uses (packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts#HTML_PAGE_SOURCE_COMPILE), so an active save or a publish of a faulting html page answers 422 INVALID_METADATA carrying the compile diagnostics, and nothing is served. The 'HTML page failed to compile (N)' panel is therefore reachable only in the page designer's DRAFT preview, where a ?mode=draft save of the faulting source is admitted and rendered (QA run #23166)

none of showcase_command_center_jsx / showcase_capability_map / showcase_crm_workbench is in objectui e2e/live/showcase-smoke.spec.ts's SURFACES sweep — there is no automated render-clean pin for the html/react tiers, so this item is browser-driven (not marked `automated`).

degradation: (a) html — save a faulting html source at the ACTIVE door (or publish one) and capture the 422 INVALID_METADATA with its compile diagnostics; then save the same source as a ?mode=draft draft IN A WRITABLE PACKAGE (?package=PKG) that also holds an app whose navigation references the page, and open it in Studio at /_console/studio/PKG/interfaces?surface=page:NAME, where the draft preview's 'HTML page failed to compile (N)' panel renders with the diagnostic messages. An env-wide (package-less) draft has no Studio surface, and the save gate keeps a faulting html page off the rendered route, so the panel cannot be met anywhere else (knownGaps[0]); (b) react — a react runtime error shows the 'React page error' fallback on the rendered page. acceptance.verify: the KPI number equals the live showcase_project count, and the network carries the find query the page's useEffect issues
acceptance.evidence: the KPI screenshot + the data read (match) + the find-query network trace

acceptance.clause: react HANDLERS run (execution, not a parsed tree): selecting a ListView row binds the ObjectForm to that record and '+ New project' switches the form to create mode — React state transitions the html tier could never express
acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms render, a ref-targeted row click updates the form to the selected record; the New button switches modes

knownGaps: THE POSITIVE ENTRY LEG NEEDS A PLANTED ROW, AND ONE CAN BE PLANTED ON AN ISOLATED SCRATCH FILE DB (QA run #24604): every authoring door validates at save (the 422 gate studio-authoring.authoring-validation-not-persisted proves), so a stock store holds NO invalid item and the sweep legitimately answers clean — entries:[], total:0 — and sys_metadata is a storage table, not a data-plane object, so /api/v1/data cannot plant one. The recipe: save a VALID view through the door WITH ?package=<a writable package> (DirectoryPage is always package-scoped, so a package-less row never reaches a tile badge), then rewrite that row's sys_metadata.metadata in the scratch SQLite file (e.g. config.columns[0].field = 123); the next sweep reports it with no restart, and deleting the row restores a clean sweep. ⛔ Only on the run's own file DB, never a shared one. The located-error half is also unit-pinned at the producer: packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.union-issues.test.ts (computeMetadataDiagnostics names the offending key per union branch, and decorateMetadataItem carries it). That pin scores neither the sweep entry nor the page's deep link

items.title: A picklist authored in a package is used by two objects' select fields from the designer: both forms offer its options, the bound field refuses inline options, and a GET → edit → PUT of an object with a bound field saves
